method:
Task 5: pelvis, groin, glutes, legs and feet from the 66-edge pelvis opening - designed loops, no auto-remesh.

  * HIPS: horizontal loops below the pelvis opening (z = 0.915) down to the last level where the body is one loop
    (just above the crotch). Each loop is a cut of the source, split at the midline (x = 0), and each half carries 33
    edges placed at the same arc-length fractions as the opening, so the columns run on from the torso.
  * CROTCH: a 7-edge midline strip under the crotch from the front midline vertex of the last hip loop to the back
    midline vertex, traced by rays fanned in the midline plane. Both legs share it, so each leg's first ring is
    33 (its half of the hip loop) + 7 = 40 edges.
  * LEGS (each side measured on its own): joints from the cross-sections (knee = narrowest cut between thigh and
    calf, ankle = narrowest cut above the malleoli); a centre line made of the thigh line (upper-thigh centroid -> knee), a rounded corner at the
    knee, the shank line, a rounded corner at the ankle and the measured forefoot line (slice centroids). 40-vertex
    rings perpendicular to it (denser at the knee and ankle), vertices placed by rays from the centre line; ring
    angles are carried along the curve (parallel transport) so the front of the leg becomes the top of the foot.
    The first rings blend from the crotch ring's vertex angles to even angles. Inner-thigh vertices never cross the
    midline (the source thighs nearly touch).
  * FOOT: dense bend rings sweep over the heel; the foot rings end at the toe bases (74 % of the heel -> toe-tip
    length; the source toes touch, so they cannot be cut apart); three concentric loops and a 14 x 6 Coons grid, projected horizontally along heel -> toe tip (the
    toes lie flat and point that way, not along the sloping, out-turned forefoot axis), cover the toes (all quads). Toes are not separated (left to the normal map; documented).
